title: Resource-aware SLIs and hotspot tracing for analytics ingestion
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce investigation time for analytics ingestion incidents and contain per-tenant cost by introducing resource-aware SLIs, adaptive trace sampling, and hotspot detection for the console analytics ingestion pipeline.

Background: The analytics ingestion pipeline sees highly variable throughput across tenants. Current tracing is either too sparse to debug P999 issues or too dense and blows our trace storage budget. Dashboards are present but lack clear SLI definitions and per-tenant baselines. We need a pragmatic set of SLIs/SLOs, an adaptive sampling strategy that prioritizes error and tail-latency traces, and dashboards/alerts that highlight resource hotspots without overwhelming on-call.

Scope: Backend console ingestion services (event ingest workers, batch ETL jobs, and the aggregation service). This ticket covers SLI definition, implementation of OpenTelemetry attributes and dynamic sampling hooks, Grafana dashboards for hotspot detection, and an incremental rollout plan to avoid noisy alerts and trace storms.
acceptance_criteria: SLIs defined for ingestion success rate, 95th/99th tail processing latency, and queue saturation; SLOs reviewed by SRE and PM
Adaptive trace sampling is implemented: error traces and tail-latency traces sampled at higher rate; low-risk requests sampled down to target budget
Per-tenant hotspot dashboard in Grafana that surfaces top 10 tenants by CPU, memory, and ingestion error rate
Alerts configured: (1) sustained queue saturation > 80% for 5m, (2) P99 processing latency regression > 2x baseline for 10m, (3) runaway trace volume growth > 30% day-over-day
Load and regression tests demonstrating trace volume is within budget at 2x baseline traffic after sampling enabled
Rollout to 5% -> 20% -> 100% tenants with automatic rollback on defined failure modes
tasks: Design SLI expressions and storage format (Prometheus/TSDB metrics and labels) - draft in Confluence
Add OpenTelemetry spans/attributes in ingest workers for queue wait, processing_time_ms, tenant_id, event_type
Implement dynamic sampling service: inputs (throughput, error rate, latency), outputs (per-tenant sample rate) and integrate sampling hook into tracer
Create Grafana dashboards and alert rules; add templating for tenant quick-select
E2E load tests and trace budget verification in staging using synthetic high-cardinality tenants
Write runbook for on-call: alert triage steps, sampling rollback, and safe patching flow
updates: 2026-03-06: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Observability, and Console backend. Agreed on three primary SLIs (success_rate, p95_processing_latency_ms, queue_fill_ratio). Action: Aisha to author SLI draft.

2026-03-08: Prototype sampling hook implemented in ingest-worker branch. Sampling decision is now a deterministic hash of tenant_id + request_id with adjustable rate. Initial tests show 8% reduction in trace events at low sampling, 62% retention for error traces.
2026-03-10: Design review feedback (Luke and Priya): require per-tenant override API and a backpressure signal from the aggregator. Added dependency on aggregator metrics (ENG-18801).

2026-03-12: Grafana dashboard mockups uploaded to Confluence; PM requested a per-route breakdown panel and an alert noise budget indicator. Created draft dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ABC123/ingest-hotspots

2026-03-13: PR opened for instrumentation changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-backend/pull/7423. Requesting review from backend and observability leads. Current blocker: choosing default sampling policy for high-cardinality tenants.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive sampling reduces cost but can mask rare concurrency bugs. Mitigation: keep sampled traces for error/tail latency and maintain a small circular buffer of recent full traces per tenant.
We will ship sampling configuration as a feature-flagged service and expose overrides to solutions-eng for large customers during rollout.
If trace storage spikes after rollout, rollback to previous sampling rates and throttle new tenants until root cause determined.
